title: Add a camera bar widget that shows when a webcam is in use
head: e8e6eff5bbca
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Relay writer can satisfy fuser without a viewer, so an idle Cam Link can show busy when its writer is visible to the probe
leads.consequence: An active relay opens the virtual output in its v4l2sink regardless of any app capture. When the shell user's fuser can inspect that process's fd (e.g. a user-run relay or privileged fuser), the command exits 0 and the widget shows the recording mark continuously, even with no PipeWire link or reader. The normal packaged relay is a system unit running as root, so unprivileged fuser may NOT be able to see it: do not claim this is reproducible on every stock installation. The existing tests model a relay whose output writer is invisible to fuser and miss the other legitimate visibility condition. On the next tick it stays busy while the writer is visible.
leads.triage: corroborated_conditional_not_published; Opus final: stock relay runs as root; user fuser skips unreadable /proc/PID/fd (fuser.c L1631-1635). Draft states idle result with basis.

leads.summary: Active relay instance without per-instance CARD_LABEL is silently omitted despite inherited default label
leads.consequence: The packaged unit loads /etc/default/v4l2-relayd first, then its optional /etc/v4l2-relayd.d/%i.conf. An instance config specifying e.g. VIDEOSRC but no CARD_LABEL can inherit Virtual Camera and stream to a loopback named Virtual Camera. The probe reads only the instance file, skips the running instance at line 155 and excludes its v4l2loopback PipeWire node. With no other webcam pw-dump succeeds yet stdout is absent, making the enabled widget disappear; subsequent ticks repeat. Omarchy's stock camlink.conf explicitly sets CARD_LABEL, so this applies to valid customised/other instances, not the stock Cam Link install. Resolve the effective systemd EnvironmentFile label (including the inherited default) or scope scanning to the known Cam Link config if supporting generic instances is not intended.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus S14; published inside N2.

leads.summary: Open #12972 adds a different Camera widget under the same omarchy.camera ID and same paths
leads.consequence: #12972 creates Camera.manifest.json and Camera.qml with the identical ID but adds a USB-camera on/off switch and a watch-based status collector. The branches are diverged, not stacked. Git cannot merge both new Camera.qml files automatically; resolving by keeping either one drops the other's camera-status or disable-toggle behavior, and duplicating manifests under different paths with the same ID fails the existing plugin registry uniqueness rule. Coordinate or integrate the two widgets before both land. GitHub reports #12972 MERGEABLE against its current base, which says nothing about the simultaneous merge. No unresolved merged test was treated as passing.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator_published; gh api pulls/12972 open head 8543c41 adds Camera.manifest.json id omarchy.camera and Camera.qml; plugins-test.sh L113 unique ids. Published as N3.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13019#issuecomment-5822793360) of `3d23957`, checked against `e8e6eff`.

**Verified:** the new commit resolves the Cam Link loopback finding and the hung-`pw-dump` timing note. No regressions were found for ordinary webcams, the `pw-dump` failure and timeout fallback, screen sharing or cloning. One test gap and two smaller notes follow, plus an overlapping open PR.

| Earlier point | Status on `e8e6eff` |
|---|---|
| Cam Link loopback depends on when PipeWire first saw the device | Resolved (details below) |
| Hung-`pw-dump` case measured time since the test started | Resolved. With 3 seconds added before that case, the new `elapsed=$((SECONDS - start))` passes and the old form fails. |
| Polling cost | Still unmeasured. On machines with a `/etc/v4l2-relayd.d/*.conf` file, each bar now also runs `systemctl is-active` per relay config every second when `pw-dump` answers; other machines run nothing new. |
| Clone, device scope, `pw-dump` timeout, test stubs, enable command, manual table | Resolved earlier and still resolved |

### Cam Link loopback: resolved

Loopback nodes no longer count as ordinary webcams. A loopback counts only while `v4l2-relayd@<name>.service` is active for a `/etc/v4l2-relayd.d/<name>.conf`. The device is found by matching that config's `CARD_LABEL` against the loopback's sysfs `name`, or else from the PipeWire node's path. This matches Omarchy's Cam Link install (`camlink.conf`, the "Cam Link 4K" label, `v4l2-relayd@camlink`), and also the `ipu7` relay installed by the `intel-ipu7-camera` package.

Sandboxed runs of the probe with stub `pw-dump`, `fuser` and `systemctl` and synthetic relay and sysfs trees:

| Scenario | `3d23957` | `e8e6eff` |
|---|---|---|
| Unplugged: config and sysfs name kept, relay stopped, leftover PipeWire node | idle (camera shown) | absent |
| Relay running, PipeWire never created a node | absent | idle |
| Same, with a process holding `/dev/video2` | absent | busy |
| Relay running, node present, not linked / linked | idle / busy | idle / busy |

The relay keeps the loopback open for writing while it runs, but it is a system service running as root, and `fuser` run as the desktop user skips processes whose file descriptors it cannot read. An unused Cam Link therefore reads idle rather than busy. This last point is traced in the v4l2-relayd and psmisc sources and was not run on hardware.

**Optional test improvement:** the "loopback source left behind after unplug" case at [`camera-widget-test.sh#L365-L368`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e8e6eff5bbcaf6a46ef8e472eadd179b3bc88355/test/shell.d/camera-widget-test.sh#L365-L368) runs with no relay config at all, while a real unplug keeps the config and only stops the service. So the new `systemctl is-active` check at [`camera-busy.sh#L147`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e8e6eff5bbcaf6a46ef8e472eadd179b3bc88355/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L147) is never exercised with a stopped relay. With its `|| continue` changed to `|| true`, the whole test still passes, and that copy reports `idle` instead of `absent` for the realistic unplug state. A case that calls `add_relay camlink "Cam Link 4K" /dev/video2`, then empties `$tmp/active-relays` (since `add_relay` marks the relay active), runs `PROBE_KEEP_RELAYS=1 probe "$tmp/loopback.json"` and expects `absent` would cover it. That case passes on this head and fails with the `|| true` copy.

**Optional:** v4l2loopback's world-readable sysfs `state` file reads `capture` while a writer is streaming into the device, which is the same condition that makes an exclusive-caps loopback a capture device. Reading it for each loopback could replace the `systemctl` call and the config parsing. It would also count other writers, such as an OBS virtual camera. Traced in source only, not tested.

### Loopbacks without a matching relay instance no longer count

On `3d23957` any loopback `Video/Source` node counted as a camera. Now a loopback counts only through an active `v4l2-relayd@` instance whose own config sets `CARD_LABEL`. These cases now read as no camera:

- an OBS virtual camera being read by an app;
- a relay instance name containing a dot, which the `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` check at line 146 skips although systemd allows it;
- an instance config that leaves `CARD_LABEL` to v4l2-relayd's default in `/etc/default/v4l2-relayd`.

**Impact:** in these setups the widget shows no camera even while the loopback is in use. Omarchy's own Cam Link and IPU7 setups are not affected, and excluding virtual cameras may well be intended.

**Suggested change:** if it is intended, a sentence in the script header or the manual would make it explicit.

### Overlapping open PR

Open PR #12972 ("Add a camera bar widget that turns every USB camera off") also adds `shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Camera.manifest.json` and `Camera.qml`, with the same `omarchy.camera` ID and different behaviour (a camera on/off toggle).

**Impact:** the two PRs add the same file paths, so their contents conflict, and `test/shell.d/plugins-test.sh` requires plugin IDs to be unique, so the two widgets cannot coexist under one ID.

**Suggested change:** coordinate with #12972, either by combining the two widgets or by giving one of them a distinct ID and file names.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of `e8e6eff` against `3d23957`, with the PipeWire 1.6.9, WirePlumber 0.5.17, v4l2loopback 0.15.4, v4l2-relayd 0.2.0 and psmisc 23.7 sources, systemd's `is-active`, and Omarchy's Cam Link and `intel-ipu7-camera` setups. Sandboxed runs of the PR's camera test, altered copies of the probe and test, and the probe with synthetic `pw-dump`, relay and sysfs data. Not tested: webcam or Cam Link hardware, a live PipeWire or systemd session (including whether the relay stops on unplug), the rendered widget, and per-tick CPU cost.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
